size.note: Shoulder height of 54–62 cm and head-and-body length of 67–100 cm follow Wikipedia. The tail is given as around 30 cm, which is a typical value rather than a range and is omitted as a range field. Wikipedia's introduction gives mass as approximately 9–18 kg, while the body of the article gives 8–18 kg, with females usually lighter; Animal Diversity Web gives 9–18 kg in males and 9–13 kg in females, and an average mass of 14 kg. The 8–18 kg range is entered, and the disagreement is noted.

summary: A slender, long-legged spotted cat with a small head, very large ears and a short, black-tipped tail. It often hunts in tall grass or near water, locating prey by ear and pouncing with a high leap.
description: The serval has the longest legs of any cat relative to its body size, a small head and large, rounded ears. The coat is golden-yellow to buff, boldly marked with black spots and stripes: lines on the head and neck break into spots on the body, which elongate and form rings on the tail. The tail is short and black-tipped. The back of the ears is black with a white bar. The underside and parts of the face are white. Melanistic animals have been recorded. It is much smaller than a cheetah or a leopard, but clearly larger than an African wild cat.
habits: Solitary, and active both by day and at night. It hunts mainly by hearing, often in tall grass or along wetlands, and leaps more than 2 m into the air to land on prey with the forefeet, killing with a bite to the neck or head. Both sexes hold overlapping home ranges of about 10–32 km² and mark them with faeces and saliva. Although it is often described as a wetland specialist, the EWT assessment notes that some of the largest populations are in areas with few wetlands, including Kruger.

diet.summary: A carnivore that feeds mainly on rodents, especially vlei rats where they occur, and also takes small birds, frogs, insects and reptiles. It locates prey by hearing and captures it with a high pounce.

young: Gestation is two to three months. A litter of one to four kittens is born, they are weaned at about one month, and they begin to hunt on their own at about six months. Mating may occur once or twice a year, at different times in different parts of the range. No Kruger-specific birth-month range was found.
habitat: Grassland, wetland edges, moorland and other cover near water, but it can live away from wetlands where there is enough grass or tree cover. In Kruger it occurs in a park with relatively few wetlands, and is sometimes seen on roads at dawn or dusk or on night drives.

similar.note: The cheetah is much larger and slimmer in a running build, with solid spots, a long ringed tail and black tear-marks; it lacks the serval's very large ears and short tail.
The leopard is much larger, with rosettes rather than a mix of bold spots and neck stripes, and it has small rounded ears and a long tail.
The African wild cat is smaller, short-legged by comparison, and has a faintly striped sandy-grey coat, not a boldly spotted one, and no oversized ears.
The caracal has a plain reddish coat and long black ear tufts, not a spotted coat and large rounded ears.

population.notes: No Kruger population figure was found. The EWT 2025 assessment notes that some of the largest populations are in areas with few wetlands, including Kruger (citing Pienaar et al. 1996), but it does not give a count. The regional status is Near Threatened, with a suspected continuing decline linked to wetland loss and incidental killing.
